correctness.rationale: On the smooth curve at a coordinate vertex, t is a uniformizer and the Gauss coordinates have exact orders q and (q+1)^2+1. Their gcd is 1 for q odd. No different monomials in these coordinates can share a valuation below q((q+1)^2+1), which exceeds the conductor (q-1)(q+1)^2 of the generated numerical semigroup. Hence the complete plane-branch semigroup equals this two-generator semigroup, and the usual gap count gives delta. The tangent line is tangent at only one preimage. The independent exact formal-series program was executed for q=3,5,7,9; the proof is uniform and not an extrapolation.

value.rationale: The three geometrically canonical fundamental-triangle flexes on smooth minimal-degree plane-filling curves lead to genuine wild dual cusps. Their complete numerical semigroup, conductor and delta invariant measure an otherwise hidden local singularity contribution across all odd prime powers; neither arbitrary examples nor the known tangent contact alone provide these invariants. The Frobenius orbit distinguishes finite-field versus geometrically split presentations.
